title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

East Devon Permanent Salary up to £27,500

We're working exclusively with a long-established and highly respected East Devon business to recruit an Accounts Assistant to join its friendly finance team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop a broad range of finance skills within a supportive and collaborative environment. The successful candidate will play a key role in the day-to-day running of the finance function, with responsibilities spanning purchase ledger, payroll support, credit control and month-end activities.

You'll be joining a business that values its people, embraces innovation, and actively invests in the development and progression of its staff.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing the purchase ledger process, ensuring supplier invoices are processed accurately and efficiently.
- Reviewing invoice data, investigating discrepancies and ensuring transactions are correctly authorised and coded.
- Maintaining positive relationships with suppliers and resolving account queries promptly.
- Assisting with supplier payment runs and ensuring payments are made in line with agreed terms.
- Providing support with credit control activities and customer account administration.
- Assisting with payroll administration and related finance processes.
- Supporting month-end reporting through reconciliations, data preparation and financial analysis.
- Contributing to continuous improvement initiatives, helping to streamline processes and maximise the use of technology.
- Providing general support across the finance team and assisting with ad hoc projects as required.

What we're looking for

To be successful in this role, you'll have:
- Previous experience in a finance, accounts or bookkeeping position.
- The ability to manage your workload effectively and meet deadlines.
- A positive, proactive attitude and willingness to learn.
- Good knowledge of Microsoft Excel
- Ability to learn new systems promptly
- A team-focused approach and a desire to contribute to a supportive working environment.

What's on Offer?
- Opportunity to gain exposure across multiple areas of finance.
- Generous holiday entitlement, increasing with service.
- Enhanced pension contributions.
- Subsidised on-site facilities and free parking.
- A supportive, family-oriented culture with genuine opportunities for development and progression.

How to Apply

Applications will be reviewed as suitable candidates are identified, so early applications are encouraged.

For more information, please contact Stefanie Farber at or apply with a current CV.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
An excellent opportunity for an ambitious Accounts Assistant to join a growing business and receive direct mentoring from an experienced Finance Director. This role offers hands-on exposure across multiple areas of finance, alongside a clear pathway to progress your accounting career

Client Details

Our client is a growing and well-established organisation looking to invest in the next generation of finance talent. They pride themselves on providing a supportive environment where junior finance professionals can develop their technical skills, gain broad accounting exposure, and receive genuine mentorship from experienced finance leaders.

Description

Reporting directly to the Finance Director, the Accounts Assistant will support the day-to-day finance function while developing their accounting knowledge and practical experience.

Key responsibilities include:
- Processing sales and purchase ledger transactions
- Posting journals and maintaining accurate accounting records
- Performing bank, supplier, and customer reconciliations
- Supporting payroll administration and wage processing
- Managing invoices, expenses, and payment runs
- Allocating receipts and resolving account queries
- Assisting with month-end reporting and financial close activities
- Supporting the wider finance team with administrative and accounting tasks
- Maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring data integrity

This role offers exposure to a broad range of accounting responsibilities, providing an excellent foundation for someone looking to build a long-term career in finance.

Profile

The successful candidate will be a motivated and ambitious finance professional with approximately one year's experience within an accounts, finance, or bookkeeping environment.

You will possess:
- Around 1 year's experience in an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, Bookkeeper, or similar role
- A basic understanding of double-entry bookkeeping, including debits and credits
- Experience with reconciliations, journals, and transactional finance processes
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills
- Good Microsoft Excel skills
- A proactive attitude and willingness to learn
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively
- Either be studying ACCA or have a desire to commence ACCA studies

Job Offer
- Permanent Accounts Assistant position based in Brent/Wembley.
- Salary of £27,000 to £30,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Direct mentorship and training from an experienced Finance Director
- Broad exposure across multiple areas of accounting and finance
- Clear progression opportunities as your responsibilities develop
- A supportive and collaborative working environment

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Are you an experienced Accounts professional looking for a role that offers both flexibility and long-term stability? Join a growing business in a thriving manufacturing and distribution sector, where your finance expertise will be valued and where a 4 day working week is available (with up to 35 hours also considered).

Job Title: Accounts Assistant
Location: Cullompton, Devon
Salary: 28,000 - 32,000 FTE
Hours: 28 - 35 hours per week, worked across 4 or 5 days, with flexibility around start and finish times.
Benefits:

23 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, increasing by 1 day per year of service up to 28 days

Free on-site parking

4% employer contributory pension scheme

Join a thriving and resilient industry with excellent long-term career stability

The Company

Our client is a growing organisation within the manufacturing and distribution sector. They pride themselves on delivering high-quality products and maintaining strong relationships with both customers and suppliers. Due to continued growth, they are looking to recruit an Accounts Assistant to join their finance team.

The Role

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and detail-focused individual to join a busy finance department. You will be responsible for managing the purchase ledger function, ensuring supplier invoices are processed accurately, maintaining supplier accounts, and supporting wider finance activities. The role also offers exposure to finance systems, reporting, reconciliations and cross-departmental support.

Key Duties
- Process supplier invoices, matching quantities, prices and VAT before posting to the accounts system.
- Investigate and report invoice discrepancies, liaising with internal stakeholders and suppliers.
- Monitor outstanding supplier invoices and proactively chase where required.
- Post overhead invoices and ensure payment deadlines are accurately maintained.
- Set up new supplier accounts and verify supplier bank details.
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve any account queries.
- Process employee expenses and verify supporting documentation.
- Post supplier payments and issue remittance advice.
- Manage company credit card transactions and monthly reconciliations.
- Maintain accurate filing and record-keeping systems.
- Support environmental reporting requirements and provide holiday cover within the finance function.
- Assist with general administration and supplier-related enquiries.

Experience Required
- Previous experience working within a Purchase Ledger, Accounts Payable or Finance Administration role.
- Strong numeracy skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Strong organisational and communication skills.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a small team.
- A proactive approach and willingness to support wider business functions.

Interviews

Interviews will be taking place for this position on Wednesday 18th November.

How to Apply

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Location: Home-based with regular travel across Cornwall
Hours: 28 hours per week (Part-Time)
Contract: Permanent
Reporting to: Parish Finance Team Leader

About the Role

My client is seeking an organised and detail-oriented Deanery Bookkeeper to support a portfolio of parishes across Cornwall. This is a varied and rewarding role that combines bookkeeping, Gift Aid administration, training, and financial support for parish teams.

Working closely with Parish Priests, volunteers, and parish staff, you will ensure that financial records and Gift Aid processes are maintained accurately and in line with diocesan procedures. The role is primarily home-based but requires regular travel to parishes throughout Cornwall.

Key Responsibilities

Bookkeeping & Financial Administration
- Maintain parish accounting records using the Diocese's online accounting system (OPAS).
- Process receipts, payments, recurring transactions, and restricted funds.
- Reconcile bank accounts and cash records.
- Review financial information and identify any missing documentation or discrepancies.
- Support parishes in maintaining accurate financial records.

Gift Aid Administration
- Manage Gift Aid declarations and donor records.
- Process envelope allocations and cashless giving records.
- Reconcile Gift Aid and accounting records.
- Prepare annual Gift Aid returns and related documentation.

Year-End Reporting
- Prepare annual financial returns for submission to the Curia Finance Office.
- Respond to finance-related queries and provide supporting information.
- Assist parishes with annual donor communications and Gift Aid processes.

Parish Support & Training
- Provide guidance, training, and ongoing support to parish staff and volunteers.
- Respond to queries via phone, email, and in-person visits.
- Help ensure compliance with diocesan financial procedures.

Audit & Monitoring
- Carry out internal audits, year-end reviews, and financial monitoring activities.
- Complete risk assessment discussions and produce written reports where required.
- Work with parishes to resolve financial and procedural issues.

About You

We are looking for someone with excellent bookkeeping skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to build positive working relationships with a wide range of people. You will be comfortable working independently while managing multiple priorities across different locations.

Essential Requirements
- AAT qualification (full or part-qualified), equivalent qualification, or significant relevant experience.
- Previous bookkeeping experience.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams.
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently following initial training.
- Full driving licence and access to a vehicle for regular travel across Cornwall (mileage reimbursed).
- Commitment to ongoing learning and professional development.
- Sympathy with and understanding of the ethos and mission of the Diocese of Plymouth.

If you are an experienced bookkeeper looking for a flexible, part-time role where you can make a meaningful contribution to local communities, we would love to hear from you.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Our client is expanding the current finance team and are looking for an experienced credit controller to work part time to provide accurate and timely financial and administrative support to the finance team, ensuring the smooth operation of accounting processes and maintaining high standards of financial control.

This role is heavily focused on credit control and debt management, ensuring timely collection of outstanding debts and effective management of customer accounts. The post holder will also support the Finance Team with financial reporting and continuous improvement of finance processes.

Part time, 20 hours per week. Hours to be discussed but can have some flexibility. Permanent role.

Key Responsibilities
- Ensure customer accounts are accurately maintained, and debts are collected in accordance with agreed payment terms.
- Process credit notes and ad hoc invoicing in line with company policies.
- Deliver timely and accurate debtor reporting i.e. days sales outstanding and overdue debts, to support effective cash flow management and commercial decision-making.
- Work closely with the sales team and credit insurance broker, to manage credit risk exposure.
- Recommend and monitor new and existing customer credit limits, and log decision making.
- Support the timely completion of monthly and annual financial reporting cycles.
- Initiate recovery plans with insurance company in instances of late/nonpayment.

Qualifications & Experience
- AAT qualified or studying AAT/CIMA/ACCA
- Strong numerical and analytical skills, and ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Confident communication and organisational skills, and ability to work cross-functionally
- Experience in an accounts or finance administration role.
- Good understanding of sales ledger and credit management.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office applications.
- Ideally have experience of SAP & ERP

title: Credit Controller - Part Time
description:
We are looking for an experienced Part-Time Credit Controller for a 20 hour a week role, to support a busy, large manufacturing business. The role will focus on maintaining an effective sales ledger, collecting outstanding customer payments, resolving account queries and helping maintain healthy cash flow.

This is a permanent role and you must have experience in a Credit Control Function before and the vacancy is due to expansion.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage an allocated portfolio of customer accounts and outstanding debt.
- Proactively chase overdue invoices by telephone and email.
- Build positive working relationships with customers to encourage prompt payment.
- Allocate and reconcile customer payments.
- Maintain accurate records of collection activity and customer communications.
- Investigate invoice discrepancies, short payments and account queries.
- Liaise with sales, customer service, dispatch, purchasing and finance teams to resolve issues delaying payment.
- Produce and review aged debtor reports.
- Monitor customers approaching or exceeding agreed credit limits.
- Set up new customer accounts and assist with credit checks where required.
- Place accounts on hold or escalate overdue balances in line with company procedures.
- Process credit notes and account adjustments following appropriate authorisation.
- Support month-end sales ledger reconciliation and reporting.
- Maintain accurate customer master data.
- Escalate potentially problematic or disputed debts to the Finance Manager.
- Ensure credit control procedures and internal financial controls are followed.

Manufacturing-Specific Responsibilities

Because this is within manufacturing, I would specifically include:
- Investigating invoice queries relating to purchase orders, deliveries, quantities, pricing and goods received.
- Working closely with production, warehouse and dispatch teams where delivery discrepancies are delaying payment.
- Managing accounts with regular or high-volume orders.
- Understanding how customer payment delays can affect working capital, purchasing and production cash flow.

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in Credit Control, Accounts Receivable, Sales Ledger or Finance Administration.
- Manufacturing, engineering, distribution or wholesale experience would be advantageous.
- Confident telephone manner with the ability to professionally chase overdue debt.
- Strong Excel skills.
- Good understanding of aged debt and customer account reconciliation.
- Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
- Able to work independently within part-time hours and prioritise high-value or overdue accounts.

For further information please contact (url removed)
